threads.body: [General] An explicitly configured deprecated `captureMapMessageAttributes=false` also captures no attributes, so absence/emptiness of every source is not the only condition. Include the deprecated boolean's false/default state in this precedence description.

-Captured context data attributes may contain sensitive information. Configure included and excluded patterns to limit the data exported as log attributes.
+`MapMessage` attributes are selected the same way, with the same pattern syntax, case sensitivity,
+and precedence. Only a non-empty selector set with `setMapMessageAttributes(IncludeExclude)` takes

replies.body:
Fixed in 5e6ca513c2. You're right that the `only when every one of these sources is absent or empty` phrasing was wrong — it implied capture-nothing requires every source to be unconfigured, when an explicit `captureMapMessageAttributes=false` produces the same result. The sentence now reads:

> No `MapMessage` attributes are captured when the selector and the pattern settings are absent or empty and `captureMapMessageAttributes` is `false`, which is also its default.

Worth noting the underlying reason the old wording was defensible but still misleading: `captureMapMessageAttributes` is a primitive `boolean` field, so an explicit `false` is indistinguishable at runtime from leaving it unset. Saying so directly is clearer than leaning on that equivalence, which is what the new sentence does.

I left the corresponding context-data sentence above it alone — that deprecated setting is a comma-separated list rather than a boolean, so for it an empty value genuinely is the absent state and the existing wording holds.

threads.body: [General] This condition omits the deprecated setting's `false` state: when no selector is present and `captureMapMessageAttributes` is explicitly `false`, nothing is captured even though that source is configured. Document the false/default case so the precedence contract is unambiguous.
threads.hunk:
@@ -154,13 +157,85 @@ public B setCaptureCodeAttributes(boolean captureCodeAttributes) { return asBuilder(); } - /** Sets whether log4j {@link MapMessage} attributes should be copied to logs. */ + /** + * Configures the log4j {@link MapMessage} attributes that will be copied to logs. + * + *

{@code MapMessage} keys and selector patterns are matched case-sensitively. {@code ?} + * matches any single character and {@code *} matches any number of characters, including none, + * so {@code included("*")} captures every {@code MapMessage} attribute. Excluded patterns take + * precedence over included patterns. A selector with only excluded patterns captures every + * {@code MapMessage} attribute that it does not exclude. + * + *

Only a non-empty selector set here takes precedence over the {@code + * mapMessageAttributesIncluded} and {@code mapMessageAttributesExcluded} settings, which in + * turn take precedence over the deprecated {@code captureMapMessageAttributes} setting. A + * {@code null} or empty selector carries no configuration, so it does not disable capture and + * the next configured source is used instead. No {@code MapMessage} attributes are captured + * only when every one of these sources is absent or empty.

replies.body:
Fixed in 5e6ca513c2, same change as the README thread. The Javadoc paragraph now ends:

> No {@code MapMessage} attributes are captured when the selector and the pattern settings are absent or empty and {@code captureMapMessageAttributes} is {@code false}, which is also its default.

Naming the `false`/default state explicitly is better than relying on the reader to infer that a primitive `boolean` field makes an explicit `false` indistinguishable from unset.

While confirming this I also found that the middle step of the documented chain — configuration-file patterns beating the deprecated boolean — had no test in the library module. It can't be expressed programmatically anymore, because `setCaptureMapMessageAttributes(boolean)` delegates to `setMapMessageAttributes(IncludeExclude)` rather than writing its own field, so the boolean field is only reachable from XML. The same commit adds an `OpenTelemetryMapMessageSelectorPrecedenceAppender` to the test `log4j2.xml` that sets `captureMapMessageAttributes="true"` alongside `mapMessageAttributesIncluded`/`Excluded`, plus a test asserting the patterns win. That's the exact configuration of a user adding the new patterns to an existing `log4j2.xml` without removing the old attribute.
